branch: report kappa_min/kappa_median/full ten-pair distribution for frozen and off-axis protocols, and test whether excluding the worst pair explains the 2.1x vs 3.08x noise-tolerance gap
what: Recomputes camera view directions directly from src/render_ceiling/render.py's VIEWS (frozen) and VIEWS_PERTURBED (off-axis) rotation strings via ASE, then kappa = 1/sqrt(1-|cos theta|) for all C(5,2)=10 camera pairs in each protocol.

noise_tolerance_crossing.source: si_body.tex lines 197-211 (Table S2), verified against results/option_a_frontier/results.json ck_2_1_kappa_prediction

mechanism_test.finding: excluding the single dominant pair (axis_a/oblique2), the remaining nine pairs are essentially unchanged between protocols (mean 1.3897 frozen vs 1.3430 off-axis, ratio 0.966 -- off-axis is marginally BETTER conditioned on these nine), while kappa_max itself triples (2.7321 -> 8.4258, ratio 3.084).
mechanism_test.verdict: PARTIALLY CORRECT, converts a reported prediction gap into a mechanism, not a full quantitative derivation. Because Algorithm S1 enumerates all view pairs and verifies each candidate against every other view, the typical (9-of-10) pair barely degrades under off-axis rotation, while only the single worst pair degrades severely. An aggregate accuracy statistic pooled over many candidate pairs and structures should therefore move by less than the worst-pair ratio predicts (2.1x observed vs 3.08x from kappa_max alone), which is the qualitative direction and magnitude of the observed gap, but not an exact closed-form derivation of 2.1x specifically.
